name: tbox (co/context)
workload: 10,000,000 coroutine switches between 2 or 1000 coroutines, benchbox 'switch' case, run on macOS x86_64, ArchLinux i386 and LinuxMint x86_64 (VirtualBox guests)
claimed_speedup: 1000 coroutines, LinuxMint x86_64: tbox 400 ms vs boost 894 ms vs libco 2288 ms (25.0M vs 11.2M vs 4.4M switches/s); 2 coroutines, macOS x86_64: tbox 205 ms vs boost 728 ms; ArchLinux i386: tbox 154 ms vs boost 485 ms vs libco 774 ms
hardware: not stated (macOS x86_64 host and VirtualBox guests; no CPU model)
tradeoffs: co/context is a C library with hand-written assembly derived from Boost.Context with a re-tuned stack layout; coroutine API is part of the larger tbox C library (build via xmake); stackful.
caveats: Benchmark is run by the tbox author (benchbox is a sibling repo), so first-party. Compiler, flags and CPU model are not stated and results come from VirtualBox guests. On the LinuxMint x86_64 2-coroutine run the margin over Boost is small (187 ms vs 199 ms) and libmill is faster (145 ms); benchmark is from 2016. Only Boost.Context 'boost' column and libco are baselines in the list; libmill, libtask, libgo, libfiber(acl), cloudwu coroutine and golang are extra columns.
found_via: WebSearch: tboox benchmark coroutine context switch libco boost.context tbox xmake co benchmark repository -> tboox/benchbox wiki switch page

name: Boost.Cobalt
baseline: Boost.Asio stackful coroutines (spawn on Boost.Context) and asio::awaitable
workload: Cobalt task vs asio::awaitable vs asio stackful coroutine: 50M asio::post co_awaits, 10M immediate channel send/receive, 3M parallel channel send/receive, channel comparison
claimed_speedup: posting 50M times: cobalt 2472 ms gcc12 / 2098 ms clang16 vs stackful 3655 / 3725 ms (about 1.5x-1.8x, derived from page data); immediate channel 10M: cobalt 1810 / 1864 ms vs stackful 3922 / 4705 ms; cobalt::channel 3M: 500 / 350 ms vs stackful 867 / 907 ms
compiler_and_flags: gcc 12 and clang 16; flags not stated
tradeoffs: C++20 stackless coroutines tied to Boost.Asio (Boost 1.82+); not a general-purpose fiber library and cannot suspend from nested calls like stackful fibers.
caveats: First-party numbers on one laptop CPU, compiler flags unstated, gcc 12 / clang 16 are old. Baseline is asio's spawn/yield_context (Boost.Context based), not Boost.Context or Boost.Fiber directly; it only roughly matches the category baseline. Against asio::awaitable the gain is small or nil for the post benchmark (2472 vs 2432 ms on gcc 12).
found_via: WebSearch: boostorg cobalt benchmarks page results asio coroutines vs cobalt -> doc/benchmarks.adoc

name: libcr
workload: Coroutine and protothread task switches on an Intel Core i7-8700 3.20GHz: thread-unsafe, thread-safe single thread, thread-safe across 12 CPU threads
claimed_speedup: thread-unsafe coroutine switch 335 MHz (3 ns) vs kernel task switch about 400 kHz (2.5 us); README states around 837.5 times faster than kernel task switches; thread-safe 80 MHz (12 ns) single thread, 166 MHz (6 ns) across 12 threads
tradeoffs: Stackless protothread-style coroutines for small devices (56 bytes per coroutine on 64-bit); AGPL-3.0 license is a strong copyleft constraint.
caveats: Baseline is kernel thread switching, not Boost.Context, Boost.Coroutine or libco, so it is not a comparison against the listed incumbents; compiler and flags not stated; first-party README numbers; very small project.
